newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO calm about rival SFB bid.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO calm about rival SFB bid.

text.p: Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV said on Tuesday it was not worried by reports that Standard Federal Bancorp, the U.S. savings bank for which it has made an agreed $1.95 billion bid, has received a higher offer.

Dutch newspaper de Volkskrant said Ohio-based Charter One Financial Inc had offered $47 million more than ABN AMRO, which received the approval of the Standard Federal board for its $59 per share bid announced on Friday.
"We are not worried in the least because we have a clear cut offer that came out of a selection process," ABN AMRO spokesman Jules Prast told Reuters.
"We will see what comes of it," he added.
ABN AMRO executive board chairman Jan Kalff told a news conference last Friday that ABN AMRO emerged as the highest bidder for the Michigan-based bank in a private auction.
Prast said unspecified measures in the takeover agreement with SFB meant it was not "as easy as it seems" for a rival bid to succeed.
"There's more than just an agreement. There's a willingness to co-operate," he said.
